question: How much time will it take for an amount of Rs. 600 to yield Rs. 54 as interest at 3% per annum of simple interest ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct formula for Time in Simple Interest:

Time = (SI × 100) ÷ (Principal × Rate)

T = (54 × 100) ÷ (600 × 3)

T = 5400 ÷ 1800 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 600

Simple Interest (SI) = Rs. 54

Rate of Interest (R) = 3% per annum

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Principal = Rs. 600
 
• 
 

 Rate = 3% p.a.
 Time = T years
 
 SI = Rs. 54

**Calculations:**

⇒ 54 = (600 × 3 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 54 = 6 × 3 × T

⇒ 54 = 18 × T

⇒ T = 54 ÷ 18

⇒ T = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple Interest is calculated uniformly only on the initial principal amount throughout the entire time period. The fundamental formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Total Amount (A)

The total amount to be paid or received at the end of the specified time period is the sum of the Principal and Simple Interest. Formula: A = P + SI.

Simple vs Compound Interest

While Simple Interest remains constant every year for a given principal and rate, Compound Interest is continuously calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest of the previous periods.
